2607.05319.title: Steering Optimisation Trajectories in Diffusion Representation Learning
2607.05319.paper_summary: We study why diffusion autoencoders can achieve similar image quality while learning substantially different latent structures. We trace this behaviour to optimisation dynamics; we analyse curves of image reconstruction against latent representation quality, revealing trajectories that organise around two distinct regimes early in training. Models in the reconstruction regime prioritise image fidelity early, whereas those in the disentanglement regime improve reconstruction and disentanglement more gradually. We hypothesise that this behaviour can be influenced by targeting shortcut pathways in the diffusion U-Net and controlling early noise-level exposure, thereby shaping the reconstruction-disentanglement trade-off during training. To steer optimisation toward stronger representations, we introduce SteeringDRL, combining gated residual U-Nets with a simple noise-level exposure curriculum for training. Across disentanglement benchmarks, SteeringDRL improves representation quality and reduces seed sensitivity. Our method further extends to spatial disentanglement in object-centric learning, improving segmentation quality on synthetic and real-world datasets.
2607.05319.paper_summary_zh: 我們研究為什麼擴散自編碼器能夠在學習實質上不同的潛在結構的同時達到類似的圖像質量。我們將這種行為追溯到優化動態；我們分析了圖像重建與潛在表示質量的曲線，揭示了在訓練早期圍繞兩個不同範疇組織的軌跡。重建範疇中的模型早期優先考慮圖像保真度，而在解耦範疇中的模型則更逐漸地改善重建和解耦。我們假設這種行為可以通過針對擴散 U-Net 中的捷徑路徑和控制早期噪聲水平暴露來影響，從而在訓練過程中塑造重建-解耦的權衡。為了將優化引導向更強的表示，我們引入了 SteeringDRL，將門控殘差 U-Net 與簡單的噪聲水平暴露課程相結合進行訓練。在解耦基準測試中，SteeringDRL 改善了表示質量並減少了種子敏感性。我們的方法進一步擴展到以物體為中心的學習中的空間解耦，改善了合成和真實世界數據集上的分割質量。
